title: Rate Lock Commitment Holding Limits per Borrower and per Loan File
content:
**Standard.** A customer may hold at most **2** Rate Lock Commitment locks in pending, locked or expired status at once, one per in-process loan file. A loan file may carry only one lock whose status is pending, locked or expired. A request for a different term or rate on a file that already has such a lock is handled as an extension, relock, float-down or cancellation of the existing lock, never as a second lock.

**Basis of the check.** Whether a loan file already carries such a lock is read from the system's rate lock records for that same loan file: the loan file the lock protects and the lock's status. This is checked before a new lock is requested. What the borrower says about other locks is not the basis.

| Lock already on the same loan file | New lock request on that file |
|---|---|
| A lock in pending status | Not opened as a second lock |
| A lock in locked status | Not opened as a second lock |
| A lock in expired status | Not opened as a second lock |
| No lock in pending, locked or expired status | The one-lock-per-file limit does not stand in the way |

### Points of judgement

- Locks that are cancelled or delivered are not counted toward either limit. The limits count only pending, locked and expired locks.
- *Hypothetical case:* a borrower holds a locked Rate Lock Commitment on a purchase file and a pending one on a refinance of another home. That is 2 locks, one per in-process loan file, which is the maximum the borrower may hold at once.
- *Hypothetical case:* a borrower whose file carries an expired lock asks for a longer term on the same file. The request is handled on the existing lock (as an extension, relock, float-down or cancellation), not as a second lock.
